objective: Recursively count own enumerable string keys of a bounded record tree using guarded for-in.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Own-property checks and recursive traversal remain current.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Distinguishing data from inherited names is practically useful.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Traversal scope, leaf definitions and bounds are transferable.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: The task explicitly practices for-in with recursion over records.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Inherited names, symbols and opaque arrays expose incompatible supplied definitions.

defects: Reference/junior counted inherited enumerable properties while senior Object.values counted only own ones.
The plain-object wording did not define allowable object classes, sharing, cycles or depth.
Senior skipped the requested for-in and the skeleton did not show an own-key guard.
rationale: Define a finite read-only record tree with data properties, own enumerable string keys, ignored inherited/nonenumerable/symbol keys, opaque array/null leaves, bounded depth/record count and at most 10000 enumerated key visits. Other object classes, cycles and shared records are outside this exercise. Guard Object.hasOwn before counting on every for-in board; replace senior Object.values and align hint/approach/skeleton order. Add inherited prototypes, nonenumerable/symbol keys, reserved own names, 100-edge depth and 10000-key width. The time model includes ignored inherited visits rather than falsely measuring only output keys.
